original_value: SummaryRecent technology developments have produced small and smart biomedical sensors, which can be worn or implanted in the human body. These biosensors create closed wireless networks named Wireless Body Area Networks (WBAN). The WBAN will continuously observe the physiological state of patients for both diagnosis and prevention. Those include on‐body measurements such as the Electrocardiogram (ECG), Electroencephalogram (EEG), temperature, and blood pressure. Ultra‐Wide‐Band (UWB) is a technology that has received a lot of attention due to several unique features such as secure transmission, low noise, and low energy consumption. Given the fact that the patients' well‐being might be dependent on the accurate realization of such networks, a high level of design and implementation accuracy are maintained throughout the system. In this paper, we proposed an Impulse‐Radio Ultra‐Wideband system, which is composed of static biomedical nodes mounted on a patient's body to collect vital data and send it wirelessly to a central node or subsequent analysis by healthcare professionals. The performance of this network, such as the effect of node location, the number of transmitted symbols, multiuser interference, and intersymbol interference, is evaluated. We also study the physical layer and quality of service of this proposed architecture.

result.paraphrase: Recent advances in technology have led to compact, intelligent biomedical sensors that can be worn on or implanted in the human body. These biosensors form closed wireless networks called Wireless Body Area Networks (WBAN), which continuously monitor patients’ physiological condition for diagnosis and prevention. Such on-body measurements include electrocardiogram (ECG), electroencephalogram (EEG), temperature, and blood pressure. Ultra-Wide-Band (UWB) has attracted considerable attention because of features such as secure transmission, low noise, and low power consumption. Since patients’ well-being may depend on accurately implementing these networks, the system is designed and built with a high degree of precision throughout. In this paper, we propose an Impulse-Radio Ultra-Wideband system made up of static biomedical nodes placed on a patient’s body to gather vital data and transmit it wirelessly to a central node or for later analysis by healthcare professionals. Network performance, including the impact of node placement, the number of transmitted symbols, multiuser interference, and intersymbol interference, is evaluated. We also examine the physical layer and quality of service of the proposed architecture.
